title: Initialization of the remaining record fields
statement: Let $m>0$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and choose distinct tape indices $\mathrm{src},\mathrm{dst}<m$, symbols $\mathrm{zero},\mathrm{one},\mathrm{first},\mathrm{last}\in\Gamma$, and words $u,v$ over $\Gamma$ with $|u|>0$. Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer and let $d$ be an $m$-tape configuration in the initial write state. Suppose the source tape, relative to its head, encodes the two fields $u,v$ joined by a blank separator, and the destination tape is blank throughout the specified range from offset $-1$ through the length of the joined output fields. Form the output fields from the one-symbol field $[\mathrm{first}]$, the field beginning with $\mathrm{one}$ followed by $|u|-1$ copies of $\mathrm{zero}$, then $k$ copies of $v$, and finally the one-symbol field $[\mathrm{last}]$, joining consecutive fields with blank separators. The initialization machine reaches its designated exit state at some time $t\le 16|J|+8|v|+16$, where $J$ is the joined output word; it does not reach that exit state at any earlier time, and throughout times $z\le t$ every work-tape head moves by at most $2|J|+2|v|+8$ from its initial position. At time $t$, the source tape is blank everywhere; the destination tape contains the encoding of $J$ on the interval from its initial head position through that position plus $|J|-1$; and every other tape cell retains its initial content.
